articles.description:
The "Knock on the Door" Problem


We tend to think of decentralized storage (like IPFS) as permanent. But physically, data always sits on someone's hard drive.
I asked myself a question:
Can we make data behave like a living organism that runs away from danger?
This weekend, I built a Proof-of-Concept to answer that. Meet WDP (Wanderer Data Preservation).
Instead of static replication, WDP uses a "Moving Target Defense" strategy.
 Time (TTL): Data moves to a new peer automatically every "Epoch" (e.g., 10 minutes) to prevent static analysis.
 Threat Detection: If a node detects network anomalies, packet loss, or "seizure" patterns in the swarm, it triggers an immediate emergency migration to a safe node and wipes itself.
It’s like a digital game of "Hot Potato," but cryptographically signed…
articles.title: I built a "Paranoid" Data Protocol that runs away from server seizure or censorship (Python + Rust)

articles.author: Ab G
articles.description:
The 5-Day AI Agents Intensive by Google and Kaggle was a transformative experience that reshaped my understanding of modern AI. Before this program, I only knew the basics of machine learning, but I had no clear idea of how real AI agents think, plan, use tools, or operate in dynamic environments. This course changed that completely.
A New Understanding of AI Agents
I learned that an AI agent is not just a chatbot or script, but a system that can perceive, reason, and act toward a goal. The difference became clear: a model predicts, but an agent decides and takes action. This shift helped me see how agentic systems power the next generation of AI.
Architectures, Tools & Context
Through the whitepapers and codelabs, I explored different agent architectures, the role of memory, and how tools can extend an agent’s abilities using MCP. I also learned how agents maintain context and work inside multi-agent systems—knowledge that helped me understand real AI workflows beyond theory.
Hands-On Learning
The practical labs were the highlight of the course. I built agents that could use tools, manage context, and work autonomously. These exercises gave me genuine confidence that I can design useful agents with the right structure.
Capstone & Reflection
In my capstone project, I combined everything—planning, evaluation, memory, and tool use—to build a small but functional agent. This experience taught me the importance of debugging, iteration, and responsible agent design.
A Clear Path Forward
This course has inspired me to continue exploring agentic AI, multi-agent systems, and autonomous workflows. It has strengthened my foundation and given me a clear direction for future projects.
Conclusion
The 5-Day AI Agents Intensive was not just a course—it was a breakthrough in my learning journey. It deepened my understanding, improved my skills, and showed me what is truly possible with agentic AI. I am grateful for this experience and excited to build more intelligent systems in the future.
articles.title: My Learning Journey Through the 5-Day AI Agents Intensive Course

articles.author: Marco Cadetg
articles.description:
Network monitoring tools like RustNet process untrusted data from the wire. This makes them vulnerable to protocol exploits and crafted payloads. If an attacker finds a bug in packet parsing, they could read sensitive files, steal data, or open reverse shells. This has happened with Wireshark before, and since we use pcap, we could face the same issues. This got me thinking about defense-in-depth: what if the tool could sandbox itself after initialization?
Network capture tools require elevated privileges. On Linux, CAP_NET_RAW allows creating raw sockets to capture packets. But once you have this capability, you usually keep it for the entire process lifetime—even though you only need it during initialization.

sudo ./network-tool --inte…

The AI field moves at breakneck speed. Every day brings new ArXiv papers, trending GitHub repos, OpenAI announcements, and Anthropic updates. Keeping up is a full-time job.
I built Pulse AI - an autonomous agent that handles the entire news curation pipeline:
Scraping - Pulls from ArXiv, GitHub Trending, RSS feeds, tech blogs
Deduplication - Uses sentence embeddings to remove duplicates
Summarization - Generates 3-sentence summaries + social hooks via Llama 3.3
Publishing - Auto-posts to 2 platforms
Podcast Creation - Generates podcast-style audio summaries using Edge TTS
LangGraph StateGraph for typed agent workflows
FastAPI backend with SQLite
Next.js 14 dashboard with Tailwind
Edge TTS for free podcast generation
I'm releasing Pulse AI under the MIT license. Check out the repo and consider contributing!
